# dsytri2

> Computes the inverse of a real symmetric indefinite matrix using the factorization produced by `dsytrf`.

<section class="intro">

Internally dispatches between the unblocked `dsytri` (when `N <= NBMAX`) and the blocked `dsytri2x` (when `N > NBMAX`), where `NBMAX` is the block size `ILAENV( 1, 'DSYTRI2', ... )`.

</section>

<!-- /.intro -->

<section class="usage">

## Usage

```js
import dsytri2 from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/base/dsytri2';
```

### Layout API

Takes a storage layout (`order`) and leading dimensions, like CBLAS/LAPACKE.

```js
dsytri2( order, uplo, N, A, LDA, IPIV, strideIPIV, WORK ) → integer
```

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `order` | `Layout` | Storage layout (`'row-major'` or `'column-major'`) |
| `uplo` | `MatrixTriangle` | `'upper'` or `'lower'`, must match the factorization |
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Order of the matrix `A`<br>Requires `N ≥ 0` |
| `A` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>N × N</sub> | **in/out** · Input matrix (factored form from `dsytrf`); on exit, the inverse stored in symmetric form |
| ↳ `LDA` | `PositiveInteger` | Leading dimension of `A`<br>Requires `LDA ≥ max(1, N)` |
| `IPIV` | `Int32Array`<br><sub>length N</sub> | Pivot indices from `dsytrf` |
| ↳ `strideIPIV` | `integer` | Stride length for `IPIV` |
| `WORK` | `Float64Array \| null`<br><sub>length ≥ MINSIZE</sub> | **out** · Workspace of length at least `max(1,N)` when `N <= NBMAX`, else `(N+NBMAX+1)*(NBMAX+3)` (allocated internally when `null`) |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `uplo`: Specifies whether the details of the factorization are stored as an upper or lower triangular matrix.

  -   `= 'U'`: Upper triangular, form is $A = U \, D \, U^T$;
  -   `= 'L'`: Lower triangular, form is $A = L \, D \, L^T$.
- `N`: The order of the matrix A. $N \ge 0$.
- `A`: On entry, the block diagonal matrix D and the multipliers used to obtain the factor U or L as computed by DSYTRF.

  On exit, if `INFO = 0`, the (symmetric) inverse of the original matrix. If `UPLO = 'U'`, the upper triangular part of the inverse is formed and the part of A below the diagonal is not referenced; if `UPLO = 'L'` the lower triangular part of the inverse is formed and the part of A above the diagonal is not referenced.
- `IPIV`: Details of the interchanges and the block structure of D as determined by DSYTRF.

</details>

**Returns** `integer`: status code (`0` = success; `> 0` = the `(k,k)` element of `D` is exactly zero so the inverse cannot be computed)

**Throws**

- `TypeError` first argument must be a valid order
- `TypeError` second argument must be a valid matrix triangle
- `RangeError` third argument must be a nonnegative integer
- `RangeError` fifth argument must be greater than or equal to `max( 1, N )`

### Strided (ndarray) API

Takes explicit strides and offsets for every array. Use it for views, sub-matrices and non-unit strides.

```js
dsytri2.ndarray(
    uplo,
    N,
    A, strideA1, strideA2, offsetA,
    IPIV, strideIPIV, offsetIPIV,
    WORK, strideWork, offsetWork
) → integer
```

Computes the inverse of a real symmetric indefinite matrix using the factorization produced by `dsytrf` (dispatches between `dsytri` and `dsytri2x` based on `N`), using alternative indexing semantics.

Matrix shapes are logical (rows × columns). The reference's leading dimension (`LDA`, …) is replaced by the two strides and the offset.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `uplo` | `MatrixTriangle` | `'upper'` or `'lower'`, must match the factorization |
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Order of the matrix `A`<br>Requires `N ≥ 0` |
| `A` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>N × N</sub> | **in/out** · Input matrix (factored form from `dsytrf`); on exit, the inverse stored in symmetric form |
| ↳ `strideA1` | `integer` | Stride of the first dimension of `A` |
| ↳ `strideA2` | `integer` | Stride of the second dimension of `A` |
| ↳ `offsetA` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `A` |
| `IPIV` | `Int32Array`<br><sub>length N</sub> | Pivot indices from `dsytrf` |
| ↳ `strideIPIV` | `integer` | Stride length for `IPIV` |
| ↳ `offsetIPIV` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `IPIV` |
| `WORK` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length ≥ MINSIZE</sub> | **out** · Workspace; size depends on dispatch (see `lib/base.js`) |
| ↳ `strideWork` | `integer` | Stride length for `WORK` |
| ↳ `offsetWork` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `WORK` |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `uplo`: Specifies whether the details of the factorization are stored as an upper or lower triangular matrix.

  -   `= 'U'`: Upper triangular, form is $A = U \, D \, U^T$;
  -   `= 'L'`: Lower triangular, form is $A = L \, D \, L^T$.
- `N`: The order of the matrix A. $N \ge 0$.
- `A`: On entry, the block diagonal matrix D and the multipliers used to obtain the factor U or L as computed by DSYTRF.

  On exit, if `INFO = 0`, the (symmetric) inverse of the original matrix. If `UPLO = 'U'`, the upper triangular part of the inverse is formed and the part of A below the diagonal is not referenced; if `UPLO = 'L'` the lower triangular part of the inverse is formed and the part of A above the diagonal is not referenced.
- `IPIV`: Details of the interchanges and the block structure of D as determined by DSYTRF.

</details>

**Returns** `integer`: status code (`0` = success; `> 0` = the `(k,k)` element of `D` is exactly zero so the inverse cannot be computed)

**Throws**

- `TypeError` first argument must be a valid matrix triangle
- `RangeError` second argument must be a nonnegative integer

### Status codes

An `info` status code: `0` on success. A positive value reports a numerical condition such as a singular pivot or a failure to converge (see the description). Invalid arguments throw instead of returning a negative `info`. Returns immediately when `N === 0`.

The reference documents `INFO` as:

-   `= 0`: successful exit
-   `< 0`: if `INFO = -i`, the i-th argument had an illegal value
-   `> 0`: if `INFO = i`, $D(i,i) = 0$; the matrix is singular and its inverse could not be computed.

</section>

<section class="examples">

## Examples

```js
import Float64Array from '@stdlib/array/float64/lib/index.js';
import Int32Array from '@stdlib/array/int32/lib/index.js';
import dsytri2 from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/base/dsytri2';

// Trivial 1x1 example: the factored form of [[5]] is itself, and its inverse is 1/5 = 0.2.
const A = new Float64Array( [ 5.0 ] );
const IPIV = new Int32Array( [ 0 ] );

const info = dsytri2( 'column-major', 'lower', 1, A, 1, IPIV, 1, null );
console.log( info ); // eslint-disable-line no-console
console.log( A[ 0 ] ); // eslint-disable-line no-console
```

</section>

<!-- /.examples -->

<section class="reference-notes">

## Reference notes

The mathematical description from the reference LAPACK 3.12.0 source of `DSYTRI2`. Indices are the 1-based Fortran indices of the source.

### Purpose

DSYTRI2 computes the inverse of a DOUBLE PRECISION symmetric indefinite matrix A using the factorization $A = U \, D \, U^T$ or $A = L \, D \, L^T$ computed by DSYTRF. DSYTRI2 sets the LEADING DIMENSION of the workspace before calling DSYTRI2X that actually computes the inverse.

</section>

<!-- /.reference-notes -->
